articles.title: Jose Luis Valdez arrived in America and started as a dishwasher; with $14,000 he later built his own frozen-dessert business
articles.summary: US News: José Luis Valdez arrived in the United States with ambitions that required years of hard work to realise. After joining his brothers in Chicago, he en.
articles.body: José Luis Valdez arrived in the United States with ambitions that required years of hard work to realise. After joining his brothers in Chicago, he entered the restaurant industry at its lowest level, working as a dishwasher before gradually moving into other roles. Yet the experience he gained did not make him abandon his childhood dream of running a business of his own. Instead, it gave him the confidence to take a risk. With his wife, Lucia, Valdez moved to Kansas City and invested $14,000 in a frozen-dessert business inspired by the flavours and traditions of Mexico. The early years were difficult, and banks refused to lend them money. Family and friends helped them continue. Over time, their small business grew into a recognised company with multiple locations and its own production facility.How Valdez worked his way up from a dishwasher to a frozen-dessert business ownerAfter emigrating, Valdez joined his brothers in Chicago and entered the restaurant industry. The Kauffman Foundation reported that he began as a dishwasher before progressing through other positions, including waiter and captain. The journey was not easy. Starting at the bottom meant long days and constant effort, but Valdez gradually built his experience and worked his way into positions at leading restaurants in Chicago. The experience also changed the way he thought about his future. A successful career in the restaurant industry could provide a comfortable living, but Valdez eventually concluded that he wanted to use his knowledge and experience to build something for himself. That decision brought him and his wife to Kansas City. The weather, the local community and the possibility of growth all influenced their choice.$14,000 wasn’t enough to start Jose’s business in Kansas CityValdez and Lucia launched their business with $14,000, but the amount was not sufficient to make the journey easy. According to the Kauffman Foundation, banks were unwilling to lend them additional money, leaving the couple to rely on help from family and friends. The first store opened on Southwest Boulevard in 2004. Valdez later recalled how difficult those early days could be. At times, there was so little business that the family slept in the store and woke when they heard the doorbell. There were moments when he questioned whether he had chosen the right business concept. But rather than abandoning the idea, he continued. The company was built around the idea of bringing a piece of Mexican culture to Kansas City through homemade, Michoacán-style ice cream and paletas. Traditional flavours sat alongside options inspired by Mexican ingredients and tastes, while the business also expanded its menu to include smoothies, churros, fruit cocktails and other food.How did selling popsicles as a child shape his ambitionsValdez's connection with frozen desserts began long before he arrived in the United States. According to the Kauffman Foundation, he was only 7-years-old when he started selling ‘paletas,’ or Mexican-style popsicles, on the streets, in markets and at bus stations in Mexico. The experience gave him more than spending money. It introduced him to the idea that selling something could create an opportunity. As a child, he was able to earn money and share it with his family and friends, while also beginning to imagine that he might one day own a business himself. That early experience stayed with him as he grew older and eventually left Mexico to pursue his ambitions in the United States.Growth of a small family business from a single location to an empireThe business gradually developed from its single location into a larger operation. The Kauffman Foundation reported that ‘Paleterias Tropicana’(title of his business) had five locations and its own production facility. Its growth also brought recognition. The company was a finalist for the Greater Kansas City Chamber of Commerce's Small Business of the Year Award in 2015 and was recognised as business of the year by the Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, according to the Kauffman Foundation. However, the expansion did not mean Valdez viewed the work as finished. He described the long hours spent at the business and the family's focus on finding ways to improve each day. The business remained closely connected to its origins as a family-run enterprise. For Valdez, the frozen desserts were not simply products to sell. They were also a way to share familiar flavours and traditions with customers in a new country.Why did Paleterias Tropicana become PalacanaIn 2022, the company announced a new chapter. According to the Palacana website, Valdez explained that Paleterias Tropicana was being renamed Palacana after 18 years in business. The name combined elements of Paleterias Tropicana into a single, new identity. Valdez described the change as an effort to give the business a more modern and fresh name while continuing the work that had begun with his family in Kansas City's historic Westside. The company also highlighted the importance of community support in its journey. The business had grown to 5 locations, with another planned, while operating its own factory to produce its ice creams and popsicles.The transformation from dishwasher to business owner was therefore not the result of one sudden breakthrough. It was built through years of work, a childhood interest in selling paletas, a willingness to take risks and the determination to continue through difficult periods. From an initial $14,000 investment and a small family store, José Luis Valdez and his wife created a frozen-dessert business that grew while remaining rooted in the Mexican flavours and traditions that inspired it in the first place.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Hammer-wielding Ohio man who smashed windows of JD Vance’s home pleads guilty
articles.summary: US News: An Ohio man has pleaded guilty to vandalising Vice President JD Vance’s Cincinnati home in January, admitting to damaging property at the protected re.
articles.body: An Ohio man has pleaded guilty to vandalising Vice President JD Vance’s Cincinnati home in January, admitting to damaging property at the protected residence with a hammer.William DeFoor, 26, pleaded guilty to two federal charges on Tuesday — engaging in physical violence against government officials or property and causing willful injury or depredation to US property.According to the New York Post (NYP), DeFoor is the son of a prominent Ohio millionaire family and has reportedly used the name “Julia” on social media.Federal prosecutors said Secret Service agents spotted DeFoor running along the fence of Vance’s protected residence shortly after midnight on January 5.Court documents allege he used a hammer to strike the window of an unmarked federal law enforcement vehicle before smashing large historic windows at the home.Prosecutors estimated the damage at approximately USD 28,000. DeFoor had remained in custody since his arrest and was later indicted by a federal grand jury.“Acts of violence directed against our political leaders, their families, or property, have no place in our society and will not be tolerated,” US Attorney Dominick S Gerace II said.DeFoor faces up to 10 years in prison on each count. He has also been ordered to pay approximately USD 28,000 in restitution and barred from coming within 350 yards of any residence of Vance or his family, whether occupied or not.As part of the plea agreement, the remaining charges against DeFoor were dismissed. He also waived his right to a jury trial and to appeal his sentence. Sentencing will be scheduled at a later date.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Allies bristle as sanctioned Russian finance minister attends U.S.-hosted G20 summit
articles.summary: Russia’s Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was left out of the “family photo” of finance ministers at a G20 meeting after complaints from Ukraine’s allies.
articles.body: ASHEVILLE, North Carolina — Traditionally the “family photo” of finance ministers at a G20 meeting is a dull, grimacing group clad mostly in gray. But this year’s picture may be much more interesting for some because of whom it omits. Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov — who has been sanctioned by the United States in April 2022 — was left out after complaints from some of Ukraine’s European allies as he attended his first Group of 20 summit on U.S. soil since President Vladimir Putin invaded his neighbor four years ago, NBC News has learned. Having served in the role since 2011, Siluanov is widely considered to be one of Putin’s most trusted Cabinet members. But he was given the cold shoulder by some of those in attendance at the event in Asheville, North Carolina, although he addressed the summit and met with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Bessent told NBC News on Tuesday that he brought up “with everyone that we have implemented our economic outcast policy, and that we expect everyone to come along with us.” He was referring to sanctions he introduced last week targeting countries and international entities facilitating trade with Iran. Asked about Siluanov’s response, Bessent said: “Many conversations are best done privately.” But a source familiar with the meeting told NBC News on Monday that Bessent, who sanctioned Russia’s two largest oil companies in October, had made clear to his counterpart the “U.S. will not provide Russia with economic relief until the war in Ukraine is over.” When Siluanov tried to discuss areas of interest, Bessent “forcefully interrupted and said nothing is possible until the war is over,” the source added. The pair met on the sidelines of the forum, with the discussion focusing on “Russian-American cooperation,” the Russian Finance Ministry said in a statement on its website. The ministry did not immediately react to NBC News’ request for comment about Siluanov’s omission from the “family photo.” Siluanov’s presence appeared to rattle some of Ukraine’s European allies including German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil who said the signal sent ​by ​receiving the ⁠Russian finance minister in the U.S. was “quite troubling.” “I would have wanted greater clarity from the American side that he should not be received here as a normal guest,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the summit of leading rich and developing nations Monday. Valdis Dombrovskis, European commissioner for the economy, echoed those concerns Tuesday. The European Union did not see it as a time to “normalize” Russia, he said at a media briefing. “We also have problems discussing sensible diplomatic matters with representatives of a country waging an aggressive war and which are killing civilians on a daily basis,” he added. There was no immediate reaction to NBC News’ request for comment about Siluanov’s attendance from the Ukrainisn Foreign Ministry, but Andrzej Domanski, the finance minister from neighboring Poland, told Reuters he was unhappy to see Russia represented, although he recognized the right of G20 hosts to invite guests. Asked by reporters at the Oval Office about the invitation to Siluanov, President Donald Trump said Monday: “Well, we are going to see what happens, but we like getting along with everybody. One of the reasons that I’m so successful, I get along with everybody.” And Erin Browne, treasury undersecretary for international affairs, said Monday the delegation was invited because Russia is a member of the G20. “It’s important to have dialogue even during times of conflict. We’ve had constructive dialogue around the table in the plenary session,” she said. While Siluanov has previously attended G20 finance minister meetings outside the U.S. after the invasion of Ukraine, his appearance on American soil follows years of political and economic isolation of Russia from Western countries in an attempt to pressure the Kremlin to negotiate an end to the conflict. In April 2022, officials from several countries, including then-Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen, walked out of a G20 meeting in Washington as Siluanov gave his remarks by video conference. Russia was suspended from the Group of Eight leading industrialized nations after it annexed the Crimean Peninsula from Ukraine in 2014, but has remained a member of the G20. NBC News has asked German and Polish finance ministries for further comment, as well the finance ministries of other European allies of Ukraine in the G20 including Italy, France and the United Kingdom.

articles.title: No fresh evidence after 40 years, court sets aside FIR order in 1984 riots case
articles.summary: Delhi court set aside a 2017 FIR order in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots deaths case, citing 40-year delay and no fresh credible evidence against police officers.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than 40 years after the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, a Delhi court has set aside a 2017 order directing registration of an FIR into the deaths of two men, holding that a criminal investigation could not be revived decades later in the absence of fresh and credible material.Special judge Bhupinder Singh, while acknowledging the lasting trauma of the riots, said, “Every proceeding must, at some point, reach finality” and sympathy for the loss “cannot substitute for the legal foundation necessary to sustain the proceedings”.The case stemmed from a complaint by riot survivor Amrik Singh, who sought registration of an FIR against then DCP Amod Kanth and then ACP/SHO SS Manan, alleging police inaction and wrongful arrest of his family members. The deaths of Amir Singh and Narender Singh occurred when the family was caught in a confrontation involving a mob, police and military personnel.Singh’s family faced prosecution over the alleged killing of a military personnel and a civilian, which was withdrawn in 1988. In 2005, Singh brought before the court a complaint alleging police inaction. In Jan 2017, a magisterial court directed registration of an FIR to ascertain the cause of the deaths.Judge Singh found the case suffered from an extraordinary delay, with no credible contemporaneous proof the alleged complaint had been pursued. The court found allegations against police difficult to reconcile with contemporaneous accounts. Though Amir Singh’s widow had told the Justice Ranganath Misra Commission her husband was killed by a rioting mob and praised DCP Kanth for protecting her family, in 1987, the family attributed the deaths to mob violence.The court said earlier inquiries had found no reliable material indicating misconduct by the officers, noting the absence of fresh forensic evidence, witness statements or specific acts attributable to the accused.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: After maternity leave, women have right to resume at same functional status: HC
articles.summary: Delhi High Court rules women must return from maternity leave to the same functional role, status and responsibilities; awards Rs 10 lakh compensation, urges stronger rules.
articles.body: New Delhi: Noting that maternity leave can’t cost a woman her job or promotion on return, Delhi High Court has held that statutory protection extends to her duties, functional status, reporting hierarchy, supervisory responsibilities and prospects of appraisal.Granting over Rs 10 lakh as compensation to a chartered accountant who was subjected to professional disadvantage on disclosing her pregnancy and returning from maternity leave, the court stressed that protection to women in such cases can’t be reduced to merely retaining their salary and designation.Justice Sachin Datta said Monday that a woman returning from maternity leave is ordinarily entitled to be restored to the post she held immediately before going on leave. “Motherhood cannot be permitted to become a basis for unequal treatment or professional disadvantage in the workplace,” it said. “Where a woman employee is placed at a disadvantage, deprived of professional growth, denied promotion, stripped of responsibilities, or otherwise subjected to adverse employment consequences solely on account of pregnancy or maternity leave, the resulting action is not merely contrary to the spirit of Maternity Benefit Act but is also manifestly arbitrary and offensive to the guarantee of equality under Article 14.”It stressed that the expression “conditions of service” covers the substantive incidents of employment and permitting an employer to maintain an employee’s salary and designation while stripping her of meaningful responsibilities, authority or career prospects would allow the employer to achieve indirectly what the law prohibits directly.The petitioner said she had around 14 years of professional experience and was appointed as manager, accounting, when she proceeded on leave in Dec 2023. On her return in July 2024, she was told that her original position was no longer available and allotted substantially inferior work.The employer claimed that her designation, level, salary and seniority remained unchanged and she was assigned investment accounting and currency revaluation functions at the same managerial level following organisational restructuring.HC stressed that protections under Maternity Benefit Act and Code on Social Security, 2020, stem from constitutional guarantees even against a private employer. It also asked Centre to frame rules or schemes, or issue directions, for effective implementation of maternity protections, including role and status after maternity leave, lactation support, creche disclosure and functionality, timelines for maternity-related grievances, protection against retaliation and designation of authorities to receive and decide complaints.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Texas volunteers started a cleanup 40 years ago with 2,800 people; the movement has now collected 1.3 million plastic bottles from coastlines and waterways worldwide and could change plastic policy
articles.summary: US News: More than 1.3 million plastic bottles were collected from coastlines and waterways worldwide in a massive volunteer cleanup effort that began 40 years.
articles.body: More than 1.3 million plastic bottles were collected from coastlines and waterways worldwide in a massive volunteer cleanup effort that began 40 years ago with just 2,800 people on the Texas Gulf Coast. The International Coastal Cleanup, organised by Ocean Conservancy, drew about 630,000 volunteers in 2025, who removed nearly 13.9 million pieces of rubbish across more than 15,000 miles of coastline and waterways. Plastic beverage bottles were the most commonly recorded item, with 1,338,712 collected during the campaign, while volunteers also picked up hundreds of thousands of bottle caps, plastic bags and other discarded packaging. What started as a local Texas effort has since become a global movement whose decades of data are helping researchers assess which plastic policies can actually reduce pollution.From a Texas beach to a global movement: How volunteers collected 1.3 million plastic bottlesThe International Coastal Cleanup began in 1986, when 2,800 volunteers came together to remove rubbish from beaches along the Texas Gulf Coast. Four decades later, the initiative has grown into a worldwide effort involving communities in 166 countries and territories. Nearly 20 million people have taken part in the cleanup since it began, collectively removing more than 439 million individual pieces of rubbish weighing about 184,000 tonnes. The campaign has also evolved from simply removing waste to documenting it. Volunteers record the items they collect, creating a huge database that provides researchers with information on the types of rubbish reaching coastlines and waterways around the world.The latest figures show just how large the movement has become. In 2025, around 630,000 volunteers participated and recorded nearly 13.9 million pieces of rubbish. They covered more than 15,000 miles of coastline and waterways, with plastic beverage bottles emerging as the most frequently recorded item. A total of 1,338,712 bottles were collected, alongside 885,854 plastic bottle caps. More than 1.2 million cigarette butts were also removed, as were about 581,000 plastic shopping bags and more than 1 million other plastic bags and food containers.Plastic bottles top the list of rubbish collectedThe number of bottles collected during the latest campaign highlights how strongly disposable plastic continues to feature in coastal and waterway litter. Plastic beverage bottles were the most commonly recorded item in the 2025 cleanup, while bottle caps ranked third. Over the entire history of the International Coastal Cleanup, volunteers have recorded nearly 27 million plastic drinks bottles and around 20 million plastic bottle caps.Ocean Conservancy's director of plastics policy, Dr Anja Brandon, said the continued presence of bottles was particularly concerning because they are among the most recyclable plastic products. She pointed to excessive plastic production and gaps in waste management as two factors behind their continued appearance in the environment. Increasing access to recycling, expanding bottle deposit-return systems and investing in reuse and refill infrastructure could help prevent more bottles from reaching rivers, beaches and oceans.Millions of other plastic items are still entering waterwaysPlastic bottles were only one part of the rubbish collected during the 2025 campaign. Volunteers also found huge numbers of cigarette butts, shopping bags, food containers and bottle caps. Cigarette butts are particularly notable because many filters contain plastic, meaning an item that can appear small and harmless can introduce plastic material into the environment.The historical figures reveal an even larger accumulation. Since the first cleanup in 1986, volunteers have collected more than 65 million cigarette butts, 32 million food wrappers and about 20 million plastic bottle caps. The long-running records show that disposable consumer products repeatedly appear among the most common forms of litter found along coastlines and waterways.Plastic waste can become dangerous for marine wildlifeThe problem goes well beyond the appearance of littered beaches. Once plastic enters rivers, coastal waters and oceans, it can become a threat to wildlife through ingestion and other interactions. Ocean Conservancy has highlighted research in which an albatross was found to have died after ingesting an entire plastic bottle, demonstrating how a discarded consumer product can become a direct danger to marine animals.The organisation has stressed that plastic pollution should therefore not be viewed simply as an aesthetic problem. Plastic items can remain in the environment, move through waterways and become accessible to animals. Smaller fragments can also form as larger plastic objects deteriorate, creating further opportunities for wildlife to encounter and ingest plastic.The cleanup has become a global citizen-science projectOne of the most significant developments in the 40-year history of the International Coastal Cleanup is the amount of information generated by volunteers. Participants do not simply collect rubbish and dispose of it. They identify and record individual objects, allowing Ocean Conservancy to build a detailed record of marine debris over time.The organisation says its cleanup data have been cited in nearly 300 peer-reviewed studies. Researchers can use the records to examine which types of litter are most common, how waste patterns vary between locations and whether changes in legislation or waste-management systems are reflected in the rubbish found along shorelines.That means every bottle, bag, wrapper and cigarette butt recorded during a cleanup contributes to a much larger picture. The millions of observations gathered over four decades have created an evidence base that would be extremely difficult to replicate through conventional scientific surveys alone.Researchers have used the data to test plastic policiesOne of the clearest examples of the value of the cleanup data came from a study published in Science in 2025. Researchers analysed data from 45,067 shoreline cleanups in the United States alongside information on plastic-bag policies to examine whether bans and fees were associated with changes in the amount of plastic-bag litter being collected.The study found that plastic-bag bans and fees were associated with a 25% to 47% reduction in plastic bags as a proportion of the items collected on shorelines compared with locations without those policies. The researchers also found that the reduction became larger over time after the policies were introduced, with no evidence of a rebound.The study provides an important example of how volunteer cleanup records can be used to assess the real-world effects of environmental policies. Rather than relying only on estimates of consumer behaviour or waste generation, researchers were able to examine what was actually being found along shorelines after different policies were introduced.The findings could strengthen the case for reducing single-use plasticOcean Conservancy argues that cleanups can remove waste that has already entered the environment, but prevention is ultimately more important. The organisation has called for governments to reduce the production and consumption of unnecessary single-use plastics while improving recycling and waste-disposal systems.Deposit-return schemes are another measure that could help address the problem of discarded beverage containers. Under such systems, consumers pay a deposit when purchasing a drink and receive it back when the empty container is returned. Countries including Germany, Sweden and the Republic of Ireland have established successful deposit-return systems, while the UK is preparing to introduce its own scheme.The continued appearance of plastic bottles in cleanup records adds weight to arguments for improving collection and recycling systems. If more containers are recovered and returned rather than discarded, fewer are likely to reach rivers and coastlines.Forty years of data show what happens after plastic reaches the environmentThe International Coastal Cleanup's long history gives researchers something that short-term surveys cannot provide. Volunteers have been documenting the same broad categories of waste for decades, creating a record that can reveal persistent patterns as well as changes following new policies.The campaign's historical figures are striking. Nearly 20 million people have participated since 1986, while volunteers have collected hundreds of millions of individual pieces of rubbish. Plastic drinks bottles alone account for almost 27 million recorded items, making them one of the most persistent categories in the programme's history.At the same time, the data need to be understood for what they are. The cleanup figures do not represent all the plastic entering the world's oceans because the campaign only records rubbish found and documented by participating volunteers in participating locations. Instead, they provide a vast body of observations showing what kinds of waste are actually encountered along coastlines and waterways.A Texas cleanup has become evidence for changing policyWhat began with 2,800 volunteers on the Texas Gulf Coast in 1986 has become a global movement involving hundreds of thousands of people each year. The 1.3 million plastic bottles collected in 2025 offer the latest snapshot of a much larger problem, but they also demonstrate the extraordinary scale of what volunteers can accomplish when their efforts are coordinated and documented.The International Coastal Cleanup has therefore grown into something bigger than a campaign to make beaches cleaner. Its volunteers are removing pollution, recording what they find and creating a dataset that researchers can use to evaluate environmental policies. The evidence from plastic-bag regulations shows that such data can help identify measures associated with real reductions in shoreline litter.After four decades, the legacy of those 2,800 Texas volunteers is no longer limited to the rubbish they removed from one stretch of coastline. Their effort helped establish a global movement that has collected hundreds of millions of pieces of waste and generated evidence that could help governments determine how to keep more plastic from reaching the world's waterways in the first place.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Side of slop? Bizarre AI food images jump from online to IRL menus
articles.summary: AI “slop” is now increasingly on offer at brick-and-mortar establishments.
articles.body: AI “slop” is now increasingly on offer at brick-and-mortar establishments. As AI image-making technology has grown more advanced — and cheaper to use, in some cases being free — images with a distinct “slop” flavor, namely ones with surreal or even disturbing attributes, have begun appearing on bodega, café and restaurant menus. There’s the shrimp scampi whose shrimp look more like miniature life preservers. A breakfast burrito with filling that looks more like something out of a horror movie. And “protein” options that look like they’re covered in bugs. One X user said she attempted to order an item advertised on a café’s outdoor menu only to learn it didn’t exist and was instead the product of ChatGPT. The trend comes as the use of AI has grown from a tech-employee specialty to a nearly ubiquitous pursuit among white-collar workers — and as overall inflation in the economy has remained stubborn. The confluence of lingering cost pressures and advancing technology appears to be translating into a boom in smaller businesses deploying AI-designed graphics and logos. There have been real-world consequences to the trend of AI slop making the jump from online into the real world. A coffee shop in San Francisco paid hundreds of dollars to have graffiti removed that appeared to be in response to its use of AI-generated food images on its facade, SFGate reported. “I want people to come to our restaurant, but, like, why is this such a big deal that it influences people on such intense level,” co-owner Lyndsey Lozano told the outlet. “Like, is it really that horrific that you have to act on such a feeling?” Lozano could not be reached for additional comment. Many of the establishments displaying the food images likely created by AI are smaller, likely family-owned establishments, said Paul Shovlin, an assistant professor of English at Ohio University who studies AI. He said that it may simply be the case that many of the places displaying the AI food are running on shoestring budgets. For some longtime designers, the advent of AI-related image making has been maddening — not to mention bad for their bottom lines. “ChatGPT will tell the user that their design is genius,” said Daniel Silva, owner of Silva Heeren, a longtime graphic design firm in Miami. “But then we tell them that ChatGPT isn’t giving them the right file or the right resolution and that it won’t be cheap to fix it. And they often go running.” Silva said he has seen small business and DIY customer business plunge as a result of AI, and he’s been forced to reinvent his offerings. “We no longer sell creativity,” he said. “We sell experience.” Other businesses are uploading posts to social media promising not to use AI in their design work. Jill Winger, co-owner of Chugwater Soda Fountain in Wyoming, posted a photo of her daughter holding a handwritten sign that said in part, “We will not be using AI flyers or photos to promote ourselves.” It ended up getting 119,000 likes. It follows other evidence that an AI backlash is afoot. In addition to the wave of anti-data-center political activity, Glassdoor now finds a net-negative view of AI among U.S. employees, while Brad Olesen, chief content officer at financial site Benzinga, recently wrote that his company was pulling back on using AI-generated texts in favor of human-written ones. “Search started rewarding the human byline again and so did readers,” he wrote. “We watched it show up in the traffic numbers, plain as day.” Winger said she is not a purist and uses AI technologies when she has to plan large cooks. But she said she can tell a pushback to the pervasiveness of AI in society is growing. “I’m seeing which way the pendulum is swinging,” she said.

articles.title: U.S. has launched ‘large and powerful’ strikes on Iran, Trump says
articles.summary: The U.S. has launched “large and powerful” strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, President Donald Trump said Tuesday in a post on Truth Social.
articles.body: The U.S. has launched “large and powerful” strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, President Donald Trump said Tuesday in a post on Truth Social. Trump said that the attack was “retaliation for the Iranians’ failed attempt at adding sea mines to the Strait,” adding that the mines had been “removed or detonated.” It was also in response to an Iranian missile launch at an American military base in Jordan, he said. If the Islamic Republic retaliates, Trump said, “they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings.” When that is over, he added, “there will be very little left” of the country. U.S. Central Command said in a post on X that it had targeted “Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran.” In response, Iran’s armed forces general staff said in a statement on Telegram that it would “impose a heavy cost on the American enemy.” The more the “U.S. military insists on its hostile actions in the region, the greater and heavier the losses it will have to bear,” it added. A U.S. strike hit a wedding ceremony in Kuhestak, killing four people, including a child, and wounding more than 50 others, according to the semiofficial Fars news agency, which cited the Red Crescent of Hormozgan province. Iranian state TV said the U.S. also struck a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island in the strait as well as several civilian targets in Hormozgan province. It said a fishing pier and a Ports and Maritime Organization tower in Sirik were among the sites hit. The country’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency also reported that Iran had responded with missiles and drones launched on “American bases and interests in the region.” It did not say which countries had been targeted. Trump’s post came two days after Washington and Tehran exchanged fire for the first time in a month. On Sunday, U.S. forces targeted two rocket launchers on Larak Island, home to a key port in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. strikes were the first known attack by American forces since late July, and Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said several of its “fighters and compatriots” had been killed and injured. U.S. Central Command said Monday on X that it took “limited, precise action” to prevent the Revolutionary Guard from laying mines in the crucial waterway, which 20% of the world’s oil passed through before the war began. “In essence, Iran created the threat and the U.S. military eliminated it to protect civilian mariners, commercial shipping, and the free flow of global commerce,” CENTCOM added. It was the first major military escalation in weeks in the war, which began when American and Israeli forces launched an assault on Iran in late February, killing its supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. After vowing “punishment” in response to Sunday’s U.S. strikes, the Revolutionary Guard announced later that day that it had launched attacks against U.S. military bases in Jordan. Jordan’s military said it intercepted at least eight missiles Monday. The same day, the United Arab Emirates Defense Ministry said its air force “engaged” at least one drone over its territorial waters after Iran launched drones at an air base in the country.

articles.title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Commons debut as PM
articles.summary: The prime minister's first appearance in Parliament comes more than six weeks after he entered No 10.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has taken questions from MPs in the House of Commons for the first time since taking over as prime minister.

The statement on his future plans for power comes six weeks after he took over from Sir Keir Starmer in July, just before Parliament's summer recess.

Here are the main points from what he said.

Burnham told MPs his time as mayor of Greater Manchester had given him a "clear theory of growth" that further devolution of power away from Westminster would help boost the UK's economic prospects.

But he said he wanted to avoid a "two-tier England" - where areas that have already been given greater powers pull away from those that have not.

He announced that work was under way with Cornwall council and its six MPs on a devolution deal, "with or without" an elected mayor, to help the rural economy.

Burnham's move to grant the county greater powers, without requiring it to team up with councils in neighbouring areas, could open the door to more devolution for other single counties.

Burnham also said he would meet leaders in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to explore more local powers there.

The statement was the first chance for Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch to grill Burnham on defence spending following headlines on the issue over the summer.

Chancellor John Healey was appointed by Burnham after quitting as defence secretary under Sir Keir Starmer , calling for the UK to spend 3% of gross domestic product (GDP) on defence by 2030.

However, since entering the Treasury, Healey is yet to attach a date to this spending target, and has faced pressure to do so in recent days.

Healey has said a target date for increasing spending to 3% of GDP will be set out at the next government spending review, expected in spring next year.

But in a potential signal of his intentions in this area, Burham said the arguments Healey had made about defence spending in his former role were a key reason why he had put him in charge of the Treasury.

Burnham confirmed he would attend the COP31 climate summit in November, as he vowed to "meet the climate challenge".

The annual UN climate change conference will take place in Antalya, Turkey, allowing Burnham to come face to face with many world leaders and senior officials.

While Sir Keir attended COP summits when he was prime minister, Rishi Sunak was criticised in 2022 for not going because he had "other pressing domestic commitments".

Burnham's pledge to attend the summit comes as he faces a looming decision about whether to allow drilling to start in the Rosebank oilfield and Jackdaw gasfield, in the North Sea, which have been in legal limbo for a year.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto promised to "finally bring the feudal leasehold system to an end", after campaigners said it was unfair that flat owners had little control over spiralling property costs.

A draft Leasehold and Commonhold Reform Bill published by Starmer's government earlier this year included plans to cap ground rent at £250, ban the sale of new leasehold flats and give homeowners greater control over how their buildings are managed.

Under the bill, leasehold would be banned "except in limited cases", and developers would no longer be allowed to sell new flats as leasehold.

That bill is yet to be introduced to Parliament, but Burnham confirmed he intended to "bring forward" a Commonhold and Leasehold Bill during the current session of Parliament, which began in May and would normally last around a year.

Burnham kicked off his Commons statement by paying tribute to his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, who had announced he was resigning as MP for Holborn and St Pancras just hours earlier.

Sir Keir had given the UK "a lifetime of service", Burnham said, including delivering the Hillsborough Law which demands more accountability from public officials during official inquiries, as well as work to achieve peace in Ukraine.

He also praised Sir Keir for leading Labour to one of its "best victories" in the 2024 election.

He said Sir Keir had "created a platform to change this country for the better" which the new government would "use well".

articles.title: Vanuatu pushes France to accept ICJ jurisdiction in Pacific islands dispute
articles.summary: Vanuatu says French control of islands is relic of colonial past, as France’s far right uses case as a political weapon.
articles.body:
The Pacific island nation of Vanuatu has filed an application with the International Court of Justice (ICJ) seeking sovereignty over two small Pacific islands controlled by France.

The Hague-based court said in a statement on Tuesday that Vanuatu’s application concerns sovereignty over Umaenupne, also known as Matthew Island, and Umaeneg/Leka, or Hunter Island.

The case seeks closure on a decades-old territorial dispute rooted in the region’s colonial history. Far-right parties in France are seeking to use the case as a political weapon.

The ICJ, also known as the World Court, will not immediately take up the case because France has not accepted the court’s compulsory jurisdiction over disputes with other states.

Vanuatu’s application has been sent to Paris to determine whether France agrees to let the court hear the case.

“No action will be taken in the proceedings unless and until France consents to the Court’s jurisdiction in the case,” the ICJ said.

The dispute has become part of a wider debate over France’s colonial legacy in the Pacific.

Vanuatu, jointly ruled by France and Britain until independence in 1980, argues that its decolonisation will not be complete until the islands are returned under its control.

The issue has also been seized upon by France’s far right, which has accused President Emmanuel Macron’s government of being prepared to surrender French territory, a claim Paris has repeatedly rejected.

Vanuatu has challenged French sovereignty over the islands since gaining independence, arguing that the colonial-era arrangement placing them under French control was made without consulting the Indigenous population.

Matthew and Hunter are uninhabited volcanic islands in the South Pacific, about 300 kilometres (190 miles) east of the French territory of New Caledonia and southeast of Vanuatu.

While the islands themselves are small, sovereignty affects control over surrounding waters, including fishing rights and access to seabed resources.

In 2025, France and Vanuatu agreed to new rounds of bilateral negotiations over the islands and their maritime boundaries after earlier talks in 2018 and 2019.

Earlier this year, Vanuatu said negotiations had reached an impasse and that it would take the dispute to an international court.

The ICJ, the United Nations’ highest court, deals with disputes between states and frequently rules on disagreements over land and maritime boundaries.

articles.title: Health crisis looming as Gaza heads towards rainy season, warns WHO
articles.summary: Water quality in embattled Palestinian enclave already poor; flooding will exacerbate threat to health, says UN agency.
articles.body:
The approach of winter and cold rains are set to worsen a public health crisis that already has a firm grip in the embattled Gaza Strip, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

Recent water testing has shown there is a clear deterioration in the quality of water in the Palestinian enclave and diarrhea cases have surged, the United Nations health agency said on Tuesday, noting that the approach of winter threatens to exasperate the situation.

Much of Gaza has been destroyed during Israel’s genocidal war, and it remains under blockade, leaving much of its population without sufficient shelter and exposed to a lack of functioning infrastructure.

“Whilst we fail to provide people with the minimum quantities of water, water quality and water contamination remains a major issue,” said Reinhilde Van de Weerdt, the WHO’s representative in the Palestinian territories.

Potential flooding resulting from winter rains “will [send] the sewage, the waste and contaminated water into the pl000aces where people sleep, cook and care for their loved ones,” she warned.

Testing of approximately 6,700 water samples over the first eight months of 2026 indicated that “microbiological contamination almost tripled,” she told reporters in Geneva, speaking from Gaza.

Contamination increased from under six percent in January to over 18 percent in August, the tests showed.

Cases of acute diarrhea have almost doubled since March, jumping from around 27,000 cases to over 48,000, Van de Weerdt noted.

However, the WHO official insisted there is still time to prevent a public health disaster. She called for “unimpeded and expedited entry of humanitarian supplies”.

Materials needed for permanent shelter and sustainable provision of water and waste management are vital, she said. More laboratory supplies are urgently needed to help confirm the causes of disease and better respond to outbreaks.

Israel has been using water access as a “weapon” in Gaza, Doctors Without Borders declared in April. The group pointed to data from the United Nations, European Union and World Bank indicating that Israel had destroyed or damaged nearly 90 percent of water and sanitation infrastructure in the territory.

articles.title: North Carolina climber airlifted after plunging 20 feet down gorge, sustaining serious injuries
articles.summary: A climber fell 20 feet on Shortoff Mountain in North Carolina's Linville Gorge, triggering a massive Black Hawk helicopter airlift to Charlotte.
articles.body: A hiker who fell 20 feet in a North Carolina gorge and sustained serious injuries was airlifted out of harm’s way over the weekend. Emergency crews were called around 2 p.m. Sunday amid reports of a fallen climber along a steep section of Shortoff Mountain in Linville Gorge. "The lead climber was attempting to place gear approximately 40 feet above the ledge when they took a lead fall of approximately 15–20 feet," Burke Rescue Inc. and SAR posted on its Facebook page, "during which they swung away from the climbing wall and struck an adjacent rock pillar." An online fundraiser shared by Burke Rescue identified the climber as Jacob Gregory. HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF Paramedics initially responded, rappelled down to the climber, and assessed the patient while additional resources were requested. "After a request for whole blood, a Burke Rescue volunteer ran approximately 1.5 miles, covering 1,000 feet of elevation in just 31 minutes," the Facebook post states, "while carrying critical whole blood to the patient to help stabilize them for transport." AMERICAN RED CROSS DECLARES NATIONAL BLOOD CRISIS AS TYPE O SUPPLY DROPS TO DANGEROUS LEVELS A North Carolina Helo-Aquatic Rescue Team Black Hawk helicopter was eventually called to assist with an air rescue because of the steep, rugged terrain. The helicopter, known as "Kill Devil 244," lifted the climber off the mountain and took him to Charlotte for medical treatment. The rescue involved two dozen agencies from surrounding counties. RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION "It took an extraordinary number of people, coordination, and courage to get Jacob from that remote mountainside to the care he needed," the online fundraiser said. "To every responder who answered that call: thank you. You saved a life and brought a husband, father, brother, son, friend and loved one to safety." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Burke Rescue noted that climbing comes with inherent risks and urged climbers to "know your abilities" as well as use appropriate equipment.

articles.title: Coast Guard rescues 37 suspected migrants stranded for 2 days off California coast
articles.summary: A 30-foot pleasure craft with 37 suspected migrants drifted for two days without fuel, food or water nearly 90 miles off Southern California.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: Dozens of suspected migrants were rescued from a 30-foot pleasure craft after spending two days stranded without fuel, food or water, nearly 90 miles off the Southern California coast, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. The Coast Guard said 37 suspected migrants were aboard the boat when crews reached it Friday, about 88 miles from Channel Islands Harbor. The rescue began around 3:40 p.m., when the boat’s operator radioed the Coast Guard for help. OVERCROWDED MIGRANT VESSEL WITH 240 PEOPLE ON BOARD INTERCEPTED NEAR TURKS AND CAICOS The operator said the boat had been drifting for two days without fuel, food or water and had no personal safety equipment. The Coast Guard sent several crews to the area, including the cutters Sockeye and Halibut, boats from stations in Los Angeles-Long Beach and Channel Islands, and an air crew. Crews found the boat around 8:30 p.m. and brought all 37 suspected migrants aboard the Sockeye. "I could not be prouder of the Coast Guard crews on scene who were directly responsible for 37 lives saved last night," said Master Chief Peter Nelson, the Sockeye’s officer in charge. COAST GUARD SEIZES 7K POUNDS OF COCAINE WORTH MORE THAN $54 MILLION NEAR PUERTO RICO, FIVE ARRESTED Nelson said crews carried out the rescue at night in rough conditions far from shore. "Despite operating far offshore in rough conditions at night, they persevered until every person in danger was rescued," Nelson said. "Their extraordinary professionalism, superb judgment, and impeccable seamanship shined throughout the entire case." The Sockeye brought the group to Coast Guard Base Los Angeles-Long Beach, where they were turned over to U.S. Border Patrol. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Coast Guard did not immediately say where the group was from, where the boat began its journey or where it was headed.

articles.title: Dantes jokes about daughter’s League of Legends future after baby news, viewers clash over ‘profit’ accusations
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Twitch streamer Dantes and his wife, Laura, recently announced that they are expecting a baby. The couple later appeared together on stream, where Dan.
articles.body: Twitch streamer Dantes and his wife, Laura, recently announced that they are expecting a baby. The couple later appeared together on stream, where Dantes turned the news into a series of jokes about their future daughter. He joked that they would document every moment of her life and try to turn her into a League of Legends player from birth. His comments were meant as sarcasm, but some viewers took them seriously. Others quickly pointed out that Dantes was clearly joking about an extreme content plan for his future child.Dantes jokes about his daughter's League of Legends careerDuring the stream, Dantes joked about starting a YouTube channel called “The Forlini Family” after the baby is born. He then imagined turning his daughter’s life into a League of Legends challenge, starting from the day she was born.Dantes said:“Okay, so just so everyone’s aware of the content plan: we’re starting a YouTube channel called The Forlini Family. The second she’s born, it’s going to be a speedrun from birth to Challenger. We’re hoping it takes less than six months. Every second of her life will be fully documented. It’s going to be crazy.”The joke quickly spread after an X user shared a clip from the stream. While some viewers understood that Dantes was being sarcastic, others reacted as if he was seriously planning to make his daughter’s life part of his content.One X user wrote:“Do zero people in these comments realise it's a joke?”Another viewer asked:“Do people not understand sarcasm?”Not everyone found the joke funny. One user criticized the idea of making money from a child’s life, writing:“F*****g we*rdo, all about the money... Poor child.”Another viewer added:“I'd **** myself if this was my dad ngl.”The mixed reactions came from a joke that was intentionally exaggerated, with Dantes using the language of League of Legends speedruns to imagine an impossible goal for a newborn.Dantes jokes about naming his daughter Hecarim Dantes Jr.Dantes continued with the League of Legends jokes during the stream, this time talking about his daughter’s name.He joked that the couple would name her “Hecarim Dantes Jr.,” using the name of Hecarim, the popular League of Legends champion.Dantes said:“So, guys, we’re having a daughter named Hecarim Dantes Jr., and she’s literally gonna be the most amazing League of Legends player to ever grace this planet.”Laura appeared unimpressed by the suggestion, adding another funny moment to the conversation. The clip was later shared on X, where viewers continued discussing Dantes’ jokes about his future daughter.The couple’s baby announcement itself came through a post on X, after which they appeared together on stream. Dantes then used the opportunity to joke about what life with their future daughter could look like.The comments about the YouTube channel, constant documentation and League of Legends career were presented as jokes rather than confirmed plans. The same applies to the Hecarim Dantes Jr. name, which was part of the streamer’s playful conversation with Laura.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Maine teen tied to violent 764 group is sentenced to prison for child sexual exploitation
articles.summary: A teenager from Maine with ties to the violent 764 network has been sentenced to prison for sexually exploiting children, the FBI said Tuesday.
articles.body: A teenager from Maine with ties to the violent 764 network has been sentenced to prison for sexually exploiting children, the FBI said Tuesday. The case against the 17-year-old marks the first time a juvenile has been charged in federal court for alleged crimes carried out as part of online nihilistic groups connected to the 764 network, according to the FBI’s Boston office, which led the investigation. “This first-in-the-nation case should make it crystal clear that if you conspire to commit violent, extremist crimes, your age will not shield you from accountability,” Ted E. Docks, special agent in charge of the FBI’s Boston Division, said in a statement. “What this juvenile did would shock most people to their very core, and it is our hope that by publicizing this case, others will be deterred from making the same devastating choices this teen did.” The extremist 764 network, formed by a Texas teenager in 2021 and named after his ZIP code, is made up of people who seek to coerce and manipulate children into engaging in sexual acts and committing crimes. The FBI says it’s investigating more than 500 people nationwide who have links to the violent online network, which has given rise to other splinter groups –– all built around coercing minors into escalating sexual and violent conduct. “Members of these groups within the 764 network, including groups this juvenile belonged to, work in concert with one another towards the common purpose of destroying society through corruption and exploitation of vulnerable populations,” the FBI said in a statement. “They want to sow chaos and create social unrest,” it added. The teenager was convicted of multiple charges including conspiring to sexually exploit a child, the sexual exploitation and enticement of a child, cyberstalking and identity theft. The name of the teenager was not released due to a law that prohibits the identification of juveniles charged with federal crimes. The teenager will serve a federal sentence to be followed by a period of supervised release. An FBI spokesperson said she was barred by law from providing details on the length of the sentence. “This case makes clear unfortunately, that parents must be vigilant, both to protect their children from the crimes of these extremists and to ensure their children do not fall to their influence,” Assistant Attorney General John Eisenberg said in a statement.

articles.title: When Should You Replace Nonstick Pans? | NBC Selected
articles.summary: I spoke with multiple culinary experts to find out how often you should replace your nonstick pans, and what signs to look for to know when it’s time to throw them out.
articles.body: Almost everyone you know probably has at least one or two nonstick pans in their kitchen. Nonstick pans are easy to clean and often lightweight, and there are lots of non-toxic options available today. But, depending on how long you’ve had those pans and what they’ve been through, it may be time to throw them out and get a new set. I spoke to multiple experts, including culinary instructors with decades of experience, to find out how long is too long to keep a nonstick pan, and how to know when it’s time to get rid of one. Plus, I offer a variety of options to shop if you find that you’re actually due for a new set of nonstick pans, including picks from some of our favorite brands, like Caraway, GreenPan and Our Place. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best nonstick pans to shop now All the products below are either direct recommendations from NBC Selected staff members and/or have at least a four-star average from shoppers at various retailers. A few years ago, I got this nonstick pan (from the brand to test) as part of a set from Stanley Tucci’s collection with GreenPan, and it’s been one of my most used pieces of cookware. After three years, all of the frying pans and saute pans from the set are in great shape, including this frying pan. The surface is truly nonstick and it isn’t hard to clean by hand even when I’ve made things like seared chicken or steak, though, I also love that it’s completely dishwasher safe; I’ve put it in the washer many times and it hasn’t gotten messed up or scratched at all. Plus, I love that it comes with a glass lid that has a metal handle. The glass lets me check on my food as it cooks, and the handle on the lid doesn’t get hot (just like the handle on the frying pan), so it’s easy to remove without oven mitts. Lastly, I also appreciate that the pans are all non-toxic and free of “forever chemicals” like PFAS, according to the brand. One of our favorite kitchen brands, Caraway, has a large variety of high-quality pans, pots and food containers, including this popular fry pan, which you can get by itself or with a heatproof glass lid for $60 more. It has a non-toxic ceramic coating that’s made without PFAS, cadmium or lead, and it is easy to clean by hand (it isn’t dishwasher safe). It’s safe to use with heat above 500 degrees Fahrenheit, so in addition to the stovetop, it’s oven safe and great for making something like a frittata or a crisp, which needs to finish the oven. You can also get the pan as part of a set of two, four or seven pieces. This bestselling pan from Our Place is available in 8.5, 10.5 and 12.5 inches and each pan comes with a wooden spatula for sauteing and a stainless steel steamer basket for vegetables, dumplings and more. It also comes with a lid that allows you to vent your food and let steam escape as needed. The Always Pan, which is oven-safe up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit, has a ceramic nonstick coating, making it easy to clean by hand. All of the brand’s pans, including this nonstick pan, is PFAS- and lead-free, according to the brand. NBC Selected editor Mili Godio has multiple pieces from Our Place and loves them. “I’ve had Our Place’s Always Pan (both the regular size and the mini) and Perfect Pot for several years now, and they’ve survived hundreds of uses (and multiple apartment moves) since 2022” she says.”The nonstick on the small pan and pot is still going strong. They’re also easy to clean: I hand wash the cookware so it lasts longer and any food residue just falls right off.” Our Place also sells the Titanium Always Pan, which is a nonstick, PFAS-free pan that doesn’t have a coating, according to the brand. If you want an alternative to nonstick pans altogether, cast iron is a great way to go, according to Michael Handal, a chef instructor at the Institute of Culinary Education in New York City. “Stainless steel and cast iron cookware would be the best alternatives. These are very durable and scratch resistant, especially when you are using metal utensils,” he says. “Small surface scratches may appear over time, but these small imperfections in the surface of the cookware will not affect the performance of the pans. And in most cases, stainless steel and carbon steel are non-reactive cooking surfaces.” A non-reactive pan is one that does not have a chemical reaction with food or affect the flavor of it. While a cast iron pan isn’t as easy to clean as a nonstick pan, it isn’t that hard to maintain one, particularly ones with an enamel coating on the bottom, such as this Le Creuset pan. In addition to having multiple handles, it also has a pour spout on each side for pouring and transferring food to containers or other pans. This set of Martha Stewart pots and pans is ideal for someone who cooks occasionally, according to NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans. The nonstick enamel — which is PFOA-, PTFE-, lead- or cadmium-free according to the brand — allows food residue to wipe right off of the surface and they look nice for serving when you have guests. “I’ve had these pans for more than a year now and I use them a lot, and they’re just starting to look a bit beat up,” says Evans. “I love cooking eggs in the small fry pan because they come out buttery and soft and I never have to scrape them with a utensil to get them out. I cook in these pans almost daily so my set is getting some wear (and noticeable tear) but if you don’t cook often you could have these for several years before needing to replace them.” How often should you replace nonstick pans? “The question of when to replace nonstick cookware will depend on the surface condition of the individual pans themselves,” says Handal. “Well maintained pans could last many years, while frequently used pans that have accumulated multiple scratches should be replaced ASAP.” If it’s easy to see the bottom of the pan through severe scratches, you should replace it immediately, since this will usually lead to pieces of the coating chipping and ending up in your food. How do you know when it’s time to replace your nonstick pans? “More than likely you will know when it is time,” says Tracy Zimmerman, an assistant professor at New York City College of Technology’s Department of Hospitality Management. Be sure to take notice of things like whether the coating is starting to flake, blister or separate from the base of the pan, according to Zimmerman. Additionally, while small scratches are fine from time to time, you should replace your pan if it has scratches showing the metal under the coating, or if it has a worn out appearance. “The most important sign is when you use them appropriately and food is still sticking,” says Zimmerman. What are alternatives to nonstick pans? Cast iron is one of the best alternatives to nonstick pans, according to Handal, Zimmerman and Michael Makuch, a chef instructor at Johnson & Wales University’s College of Food Innovation and Technology. “It is great for high heat cooking and gets better the more you use it. The downside to [using] cast iron [pans] is they are heavy, and they require a little more care to avoid rusting and pitting,” he says. And while they’re typically not nonstick, you can also consider using stainless steel pans, which are much more lightweight than cast iron pans. How do you take care of nonstick pans so they last? Taking care of your nonstick pans depends a lot on how often you use them, but also how you store them and what else you use with them, according to Zimmerman. For example, when you store them in a cabinet or shelf, you should layer your pans with a cloth so that they don’t get scratches from each other. You should also use wooden or heat-resistant silicone or rubber utensils with nonstick pans to help maintain them, according to Zimmerman. Also, only use your nonstick pans for medium high heat that’s between 400 and 500 degrees Fahrenheit. When cleaning, wash them with damp soft towels, do not scrub with anything abrasive. Meet our culinary experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Michael Handal is a chef instructor at the Institute of Culinary Education in New York City.Tracy Zimmerman is an assistant professor at New York City College of Technology’s Department of Hospitality Management. Michael Makuch is an associate professor and department chair at Johnson & Wales University’s College of Food Innovation and Technology. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home and kitchen appliances. I’ve written about the best stainless steel cookware, nontoxic grilling utensils and how to season a cast-iron skillet. For this story, I talked to multiple culinary experts for their guidance on when to throw away a nonstick pan. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Germany blames Russia for airport drone plot, shuts down consulate
articles.summary: The German government blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month using a drone laden with explosives.
articles.body: The German government on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month using a drone laden with explosives, and announced that it would shut down a Russian consulate among other measures. The drone was found near a Ukrainian plane on Aug. 4 and the device was defused. German officials said at the time that the incident posed a new level of danger. Moscow has been widely accused by Western officials of running a campaign of sabotage and disruption with the aim of undermining support for Ukraine and destabilizing European nations. Minister says evidence points to a familiar pattern German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said authorities found elements such as the drone configuration, components, explosives and detonator that are “known to us from other Russian hybrid operations and its war against Ukraine.” He said the device pointed to “a high degree of technical expertise” and painstaking planning, but carrying out the plan appears to have been left to “low-level” agents. Dobrindt told reporters that intelligence points to “people being involved who acted on behalf of Russian state entities,” though he didn’t specify which ones. “Taken together, the police investigations, the pattern and intelligence findings prove a Russian responsibility for the attempted attack at Leipzig airport.” Germany will shut a Russian consulate Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said that “with the attempted attack in Leipzig, the Russian leadership decided deliberately to do significant damage again to our already massively burdened bilateral relationship.” He said the Russian consulate in Bonn will be closed effective Sept. 18 and the contract under which the Russian House cultural center in Berlin is operated will be rescinded. Germany will propose the addition of more people from Russia to European Union (E.U.) sanctions lists “in the context of hybrid attacks,” step up entry controls for people from Russia and increase “pressure on the shadow fleet,” a reference to tankers suspected of shipping Russian oil in violation of international sanctions, Wadephul said. The E.U. has sanctioned hundreds of “shadow fleet” ships. The Russian ambassador was summoned to the Foreign Ministry in Berlin. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said there would be a “fitting response” to the planned closures, Russian state news agency Tass reported. She rejected claims of Russian involvement in the attempted drone attack, calling them a “far-fetched and contrived pretext” for Berlin to escalate tensions and arguing that “as usual, no convincing or serious evidence has been presented whatsoever.” Around 200 incidents blamed on Russia Leipzig/Halle is a major hub for international freight and for providing support to Ukraine. The planes that regularly use it include Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft. It is also home to NATO’s Strategic Airlift International Solution, or SALIS, which is currently operational almost every day in delivering equipment to NATO battle groups along its eastern flank from Finland to Romania and supporting E.U. and alliance nation missions. In 2024, an incendiary device ignited at a logistics center at the airport and set fire to a freight container before it could be loaded onto a cargo plane, part of a plot that Western security officials suspect was organized by Russian intelligence. The Associated Press has tracked around 200 incidents of sabotage and malign activity across Europe blamed on Russia by Western officials since the invasion of Ukraine. That includes organizing plots to set fire to warehouses, launching drones and trying to kill enemies abroad as well as stealing defense technology and carrying out cyberattacks on critical European infrastructure. In May, Russian President Vladimir Putin responded to the AP findings and said Moscow is not waging a sabotage campaign against Europe. He demanded that AP “name one proven fact.” Russia has faced many packages of E.U. sanctions The E.U. has slapped almost two dozen packages of sanctions on Russia over its war in Ukraine, targeting roughly 3,000 people and entities. E.U. foreign ministers will meet in Ireland Wednesday. The head of the E.U.’s executive commission, Ursula von der Leyen, said in a post on X that “hybrid attacks will not go without a clear response.” In mid-August, the German Cabinet approved plans to give the country’s intelligence services broader powers for actions such as disabling sabotage and hacking attempts. The planned reform, which had been in the works for months, still requires parliamentary approval. Hours before Tuesday’s German statement, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who has frequently warned that Russia is carrying out a campaign of sabotage against NATO countries, said Poland has been targeted by new acts of sabotage including arson within the past “dozens of hours.” He spoke the day after a fire broke out at WB Electronics, which the Polish government has described as Europe’s biggest drone manufacturer. Prosecutors said Monday that they launched an investigation based on suspicions of the “participation of foreign intelligence activities against the Republic of Poland,” without elaborating on what country might be responsible. They said the fire at the plant in Skarżysko-Kamienna destroyed warehouse facilities and caused damage estimated at at least 15 million zlotys ($4 million).

articles.title: A man buys Chinese jade dog for £1 at UK car boot sale, finds it in a box, later discovers 600-year-old Ming dynasty treasure that could fetch £10,000 at auction
articles.summary: UK News: A rare Chinese jade dog believed to be more than 600 years old could fetch up to £10,000 at auction after being bought for just £1 at a car boot sale .
articles.body: A rare Chinese jade dog believed to be more than 600 years old could fetch up to £10,000 at auction after being bought for just £1 at a car boot sale in the UK.According to The Sun, the 8.5cm-long carved animal, made from mottled black and green jade, is believed to date back to the early years of the Ming dynasty, between around 1380 and 1420. It depicts a seated, recumbent dog with its head turned backwards and its legs and tail curled up.The remarkable discovery was made just two months ago when a buyer spotted the seemingly ordinary object at a car boot sale. The jade dog is now due to go under the hammer at Hansons Auctioneers in Etwall, Derbyshire, on Wednesday.£1 car boot find could become a £10,000 treasureAuctioneer Charles Hanson said the discovery highlighted the unexpected treasures that can still be found at car boot sales across the UK.According to Hanson, one of the auction house's clients arrived at the sale relatively late, close to midday, rather than early in the morning, and spotted the small jade animal sitting inside a box on a stall.He described the piece as an “archaic seated recumbent dog” carved from black and green jade and said experts believe it dates from the late 14th or early 15th century.“We believe this little dog to be probably late 14th, early 15th century and there’s many ways we’ve been able to confirm that,” Hanson said.The vendor who sold the piece reportedly suspected that it was jade and had an inkling that it could be old, but the object was still sold for just £1.Chinese jade has a long history of cultural significanceHanson said the jade's unusual black-and-green colouring makes it particularly rare, while its age adds significantly to its importance.He expects the small carving to achieve up to £10,000 when it goes to auction.The auctioneer also highlighted the historical significance of the material itself, describing jade as a “mystical, magical substance” in Chinese society. Jade has long been associated with good fortune and has been treasured and collected in China for centuries.Despite some scratching, Hanson said the condition was remarkable considering the object's possible age. If the dating is correct, the dog could have been carved around the time of the Black Death and more than a century before Henry VIII came to the throne.‘Magical history’ behind a centuries-old jade dogFor Hanson, the discovery is a reminder that valuable pieces of history can sometimes remain hidden in plain sight.“This dog has a magical history from China and it’s revered by the Chinese today who, as back then, adore jade and collect these hard stone animals,” he said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Government halves sugar stock limit for dealers to curb hoarding
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Govt Tuesday halved sugar stock holding limit for dealers to 2,000 quintals from Sept 15 till Nov 30, in its bid to ensure adequate availab.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt Tuesday halved sugar stock holding limit for dealers to 2,000 quintals from Sept 15 till Nov 30, in its bid to ensure adequate availability in the domestic market and prevent hoarding and speculative trading. The move comes as retail prices have moderated to around Rs 63 a kg, but still remain elevated even as ex-mill prices have crashed by more than 20% after govt took a series of steps.At present, stock holding limit for sugar dealers across the country is 4,000 quintals. As per the new order, no sugar dealer can hold any stock for a period exceeding 30 days from the date of receipt of sugar consignments and no dealer can keep over 2,000 quintals of sugar at any time.Govt expects the reduction will facilitate orderly movement of sugar through the supply chain and ensure its continuous availability to consumers at reasonable prices. Meanwhile, govt has undertaken intensive monitoring and physical verification of sugar stocks, covering sugar mills, dealers and traders.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Israel warns it will retaliate if UK imposes sanctions
articles.summary: The UK's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband pledged on Tuesday to introduce a "comprehensive reset" of policy on Israel.
articles.body:
Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar has warned his country will retaliate if the UK imposes sanctions against it over the potential expansion of settlements in the West Bank.

Addressing Parliament for the first time as foreign secretary, Ed Miliband said he would introduce a "comprehensive reset" of policy on Israel "in the coming weeks".

He said the government would examine how to stop UK companies "financing, constructing or advertising new settlements" in the occupied West Bank.

Responding, Gideon Saar told Hebrew-language news website Ynet: "If Britain acts against Israel, Israel will act against Britain."

"If they act, I think they will be making a big mistake," he said.

Last month, Israel opened up tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes in the so-called E1 area - a strategically important area east of Jerusalem. The plans have drawn widespread international condemnation.

The development would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.

Miliband said the plans are "illegal under international law" and called them "the crossing of a red line, as it cuts through the heart of the West Bank and risks making a Palestinian state unviable".

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also warned that Israel's statement about the E1 area could "imperil or end" the two-state solution in the Middle East.

All settlements are illegal under international law and, under global pressure, Israel held off for decades on plans to build in the area.

The "two-state solution", which has received international backing, proposes an independent Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza, with East Jerusalem as its capital, that would exist alongside Israel.

Israel rejects a two-state solution. The Palestinian Authority backs a two-state solution but Hamas does not because it is opposed to the existence of Israel.
